title: Water disappearing underground
summary: Satellites that weigh water by its gravity see northern India's stored water falling, a sign of groundwater pumping.

steps.message: Setting up the investigation you chose...
Plan (structured): Chosen directly: Liquid Water Equivalent Thickness (groundwater / ice mass anomaly) over Indo-Gangetic Plain, 2003-2025.
Querying GRACE-FO Mascon Terrestrial Water Storage Anomaly for Liquid Water Equivalent Thickness (groundwater / ice mass anomaly) (lwe_thickness) over Indo-Gangetic Plain, 2003-2025...
Averaged 280 grid cells over Indo-Gangetic Plain (weighted by area) into 245 monthly values. Source: GRACE-FO Mascon Terrestrial Water Storage Anomaly.
Checking temporal coverage, gaps, and outliers...
Data quality OK — 89% complete, 20.4 years, 0 outliers flagged. Minor issues noted: Largest data gap is 370 days (over one year).

issues: Largest data gap is 370 days (over one year).

steps.message: Building monthly means, removing the seasonal cycle, and calculating the trend...
Liquid Water Equivalent Thickness (groundwater / ice mass anomaly) is decreasing at -18.06 cm per decade (Sen's slope on 243 monthly anomalies, seasonal cycle removed). Found 3 change point(s).

trend.basis_reason: Monthly values with the average seasonal cycle removed were tested, using every month of data.

steps.message: Testing significance (Mann-Kendall and t-test, both corrected for autocorrelation)...

Mann-Kendall p = 0.0000 — the trend is statistically significant at alpha=0.05. Sen's slope 95% CI: [-2.202, -1.401] per year. t-test p = 0.0000 with an effective sample size of 21 (lag-1 autocorrelation 0.84).

detail.importance_note: Effect size = |total change| / std. dev. = 12.04 — the observed change is large relative to natural year-to-year variability. A statistically significant trend can still have a small effect size; significance and scientific/practical importance are evaluated separately here.

steps.message: Sampling a spatial grid across Indo-Gangetic Plain to check for regional differences...
Found opposite regional trends within Indo-Gangetic Plain: 6 grid cells increasing, 37 decreasing (of 43 cells significant after false-discovery-rate control).
Checking 5 other variables in Indo-Gangetic Plain for year-to-year association with Liquid Water Equivalent Thickness (groundwater / ice mass anomaly) (trends removed first)...

None of the 5 variables tested moved together with Liquid Water Equivalent Thickness (groundwater / ice mass anomaly) from year to year (|r| >= 0.3 after removing trends and correcting for multiple tests).
Checking robustness of the finding...

Robustness verdict: robust with caveats. 3 abrupt change point(s) detected — part of the overall trend may reflect a step shift rather than gradual change. Largest data gap is 370 days (over one year).

caveats: 3 abrupt change point(s) detected — part of the overall trend may reflect a step shift rather than gradual change.
Largest data gap is 370 days (over one year).

steps.message: Arguing against the finding before it's finalized...
Adversarial review: held up under scrutiny, with caveats. 2 objection(s) raised.

detail.verdict: held up under scrutiny, with caveats
skeptic_points: A change point in 2009 shifted the mean by -19.56 cm — part of the reported trend may reflect a step change rather than a gradual process, which a single monotonic-trend statistic cannot distinguish from steady change.
About 11 months are missing between the GRACE and GRACE-FO missions (mid-2017 to mid-2018). Part of the trend could come from this change rather than from the Earth system.

finding.interpretation: The Liquid Water Equivalent Thickness over the Indo‑Gangetic Plain shows a statistically significant decreasing trend of about -1.81 cm per year (95 % CI: -2.20 to -1.40 cm yr⁻¹), amounting to a total loss of roughly -41.4 cm between 2003 and 2025. Seasonal analyses (DJF, MAM, JJA, SON) all indicate consistent negative slopes, confirming that the decline is not confined to a particular time of year. Spatially, the majority of grid cells (≈53 % of area) exhibit decreasing trends, while a minority show increases, suggesting heterogeneous responses within the region. The effect size (≈12 times the interannual variability) implies that the observed change is large relative to natural fluctuations, supporting scientific relevance beyond mere statistical significance.
finding.limitations: A documented change point in 2009 and an 11‑month data gap between the GRACE and GRACE‑FO missions may contribute to the apparent trend, potentially reflecting a step change rather than continuous loss. The effective sample size of 21 years limits the ability to fully resolve longer‑term variability, and spatial heterogeneity indicates that regional averages may mask localized dynamics.

provenance.statistical_method: Sen's slope with a Mann-Kendall test on monthly anomalies (seasonal cycle removed), both corrected for lag-1 autocorrelation (r1 = 0.84); OLS t-test with effective sample size n_eff = 21 as a second check

insight.headline: Falling total water storage points to groundwater depletion or ice and lake loss.

evidence.text: 3 abrupt steps were detected (2006, 2009, 2019), so a single steady trend is a poor description of this record. Repeated steps often reflect regime changes or data-source discontinuities rather than gradual driving.
Parts of the region move in opposite directions (6 grid cells rising, 37 falling), so one regional story is too simple.

drivers.title: Groundwater pumping beyond recharge
drivers.text: Where more is drawn out than rain refills, aquifers fall steadily.

drivers.title: Prolonged drought
drivers.text: Multi-year dry spells drain soils, rivers and aquifers together.

drivers.title: Melting ice
drivers.text: Loss of glaciers and ice sheets removes stored water mass.

impacts.text: Wells run dry and cities and farms lose their supply.
Irrigated farming depends on groundwater and becomes uncertain.
Over-pumped ground can sink, damaging buildings, canals and roads.
Ice loss adds to sea-level rise.

mitigate: Limit warming to slow ice loss.
End over-extraction so storage can stabilise.
Global action — one region cannot reverse a global trend, but it can cut its own share.
adapt: Groundwater metering, pumping limits and managed recharge.
Efficient irrigation and crop choices matched to available water.
insight.region_context: An intensively irrigated farming belt where groundwater depletion has been documented by satellite gravity data.
